title: Valid smoke example contains reserved public origin
finding: The file is explicitly named and commented as a smoke example, but `validate-config` accepts it while site.base_url is https://example.invalid. publishing.dry_run=true blocks live execution by default, but no semantic guard prevents a later live switch with a reserved public origin.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: validate-config exit 0; 1 source, 1 component, 1 task.
recommended_solution: Keep the fixture explicitly smoke-only and add a hard live-publish/workflow guard that rejects reserved .invalid/example origins.

title: Generic template defaults to wildcard repository hosts
finding: The unresolved URL placeholders make the untouched file fail closed. However, after replacing those placeholders, publisher.allowed_hosts and source allowed_hosts remain ["*"], silently permitting arbitrary repository hosts unless the user notices and narrows them.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: load_config accepted publisher and source clone URLs on unrelated .invalid hosts while both allowlists were ["*"].
recommended_solution: Use explicit host placeholders or restrictive defaults; add a high-visibility validation warning or strict-mode rejection for wildcard allowlists.

title: No project-level .gitignore; test-generated caches remain unignored
finding: The source ZIP does not ship cache files (verified: zero cache paths). However, running pytest/Python creates .pytest_cache and __pycache__; the extracted working tree has 25 cache/bytecode files and no root .gitignore. The post-create script also creates .venv and the harness creates test-results, so these can appear as untracked files and be committed accidentally.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: no root .gitignore; current post-test tree has cache/bytecode; source ZIP has zero cache paths.
recommended_solution: Add root .gitignore for .venv, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, test-results, _site, .publisher-tmp, .publisher-sources.

title: Devcontainer verifier under-verifies the declared runtime
finding: The image provisions Python 3.13, Java 25 plus 21, but verification accepts any Python >=3.11 and accepts Java 21 OR 25 as the active java. It never verifies that both JDKs are present. A wrong/missing primary version can still pass.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: check conditions are weaker than declared toolchain.
recommended_solution: Check Python major/minor exactly; assert java active 25 and inspect SDKMAN installed list for 21 (or documented paths).

title: Mutable Dev Container dependencies reduce reproducibility
finding: Base image tag is not digest-pinned; Java and Git LFS Features use major channel :1; Git LFS version latest, Maven version implicitly latest; apt installs current git-subtree. Rebuilds may change without a repository diff.
reproduction_or_evidence: WEB VERIFIED: Java feature currently latest 1.8.3, Git LFS feature 1.2.5; feature option names jdkDistro/additionalVersions/installMaven and autoPull valid.
recommended_solution: Pin feature versions and preferably base-image digest/package versions; establish an explicit update policy.

title: Keycloak smoke example is accepted but not deploy-ready
finding: The keycloak file is clearly called a smoke configuration and sets publishing.dry_run=true, so this is not a broken smoke test. However, it has real remote URLs and passes validation despite example.invalid site origin; it must be unmistakably separated from deployment configuration.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: validate-config succeeds; no workflow section; dry_run true.
recommended_solution: Rename to publisher.keycloak.smoke.yml or add top-level prominent SMOKE-ONLY note + strict deploy gate; keep dry_run=true locked in smoke fixture.

title: Test and CI Python versions differ
locations: publisher.keycloak.example.yml uses Maven; publisher.example.yml workflow.python_version: 3.12; .devcontainer Dockerfile: Python 3.13
finding: Development/tests run under Python 3.13 while the generic generated workflow example defaults to 3.12. The package declares Python 3.11+; there is no recorded full regression on the workflow Python 3.12.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: config defaults/examples differ; CI runtime not acceptance-tested.
recommended_solution: Run full suite on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 or pin the supported runtime contract consistently.

title: Environment interpolation whitelist is selective but not enumerated by field
finding: Only a selected set of identity/site/workspace/communication/publishing output fields are expanded. `${VAR}` in other string fields (e.g. components[].output_path, build_tasks[].argv, workflow.file) is retained literally and still passes validate-config. Design is documented as selective, but exact whitelist is not exposed in docs/matrix.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: configs with ${UNSET_OUTPUT_DIR}, ${BUILD_EXE}, ${WORKFLOW_FILE} load successfully and retain literal expressions.
recommended_solution: Publish a complete exact whitelist; reject env expressions in non-interpolated fields unless explicitly intended as literal.

title: Provider fields do not invoke provider-specific adapters
finding: Authoring/communication provider labels are accepted, but runtime uses generic templates and host checks. No GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket-specific URL logic is selected by those values. This is documented in known limits but can be mistaken for full provider integrations.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: no production runtime read of authoring provider or communication provider; docs/known-limits explicit.
recommended_solution: Rename to provider_label/metadata or remove field until adapter dispatch exists; maintain provider compatibility table.

title: Security destination privacy is self-attested, not verified
finding: private_target=true merely satisfies a semantic validator for named security channels. It does not inspect access controls or prove that the final endpoint is private.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: boolean declaration only; external endpoint verification is a release gate.
recommended_solution: Label field explicitly as assertion; require manual/provider-specific access-control evidence before release.

title: Communication schema has dynamic channels and dynamic query keys
finding: The old 218-node matrix has only a communication parent row; it omits channel field contracts and dynamic query keys. The implementation handles email specially and other channels generically. This is a coverage gap in the old matrix, not necessarily a runtime bug.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: dynamic schema refs not flattened in previous matrix.
recommended_solution: Add dynamic channel contract rows (now included in new matrix) and add channel compatibility tests.

title: The default CLI config is absent until the user creates it
finding: CLI defaults to publisher.yml, which is not in the archive. The README tells the user to copy publisher.example.yml and replace placeholders. This is intentional setup, but a freshly cloned generic engine does not run validate/plan/build without that step.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: default validate-config fails because publisher.yml is absent; generic example fails closed on placeholders.
recommended_solution: Keep this contract but make first-run state explicit; optionally provide a guided `init-config` command.

title: Historical reports and evidence are mixed into project root
finding: The archive carries many old stage reports/logs in root with prior totals (140/142/168/177 etc.) beside current evidence. Without a canonical evidence index, readers can confuse historical counts with current state.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: multiple generations of reports/logs coexist.
recommended_solution: Move historical artifacts under audit/history; one canonical current report and evidence index at root.

title: No reproducible package-install metadata/entry point
finding: The CLI is usable from repo root as python -m publisher_engine.cli, but project cannot be installed as a versioned package or expose a console_script entry point using standard build metadata. Not a failure for current workflow; it limits distribution/reuse.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: no Python packaging metadata.
recommended_solution: Add pyproject.toml with supported Python range, dependencies, package data for schema, and CLI entry point if external install is a requirement.

title: Generated workflow only targets GitHub Actions + Pages
finding: Only github_actions is generated; Pages deployment is workflow-targeted and requires artifact adapter. Other CI/hosting providers need external pipeline/adapters.
reproduction_or_evidence: EXPLICIT CONTRACT; not hidden, but must be surfaced per option score.
recommended_solution: Do not present provider labels as implemented integrations; enforce adapter/provider compatibility and enumerate supported deployment contracts.

title: Real Codespaces build and runtime not yet verified
finding: Static JSON/config tests and local checks do not prove Docker build, Feature installation, SDKMAN Java selection or GitHub Codespaces runtime.
reproduction_or_evidence: BLOCKED EXTERNAL ACCEPTANCE: no actual Codespace created from the new repository.
recommended_solution: First external acceptance must build from fresh GitHub repo before declaring R8-027 closed.

title: Git LFS integration not behavior-accepted
finding: Source-relative include handling is implemented; test fixture exists, but actual client transfer was skipped when git-lfs unavailable in previous test environment.
reproduction_or_evidence: OPEN: true object transfer remains unverified.
recommended_solution: Execute real client against local test HTTP batch/object server and assert pointer becomes hydrated bytes.

title: Process-group portability not fully accepted
finding: Linux child-process termination tests exist. Windows task tree termination path is not tested on Windows.
reproduction_or_evidence: OPEN: Windows execution acceptance absent.
recommended_solution: Add Windows CI or platform test runner for process tree timeout/child reaping.

title: CLI profile override is not uniform across commands
finding: --profile exists on validate-config, plan and build, but not publish or generate-workflow. active_profiles within the config still applies, but callers cannot override profiles per CLI invocation on those phases.
reproduction_or_evidence: STATIC: parser and dispatch.
recommended_solution: Add --profile to publish and generate-workflow or document that these phases only use active_profiles from file.

title: Keycloak example header contradicts its concrete contents
finding: The file says “replace all <...> values” and that no repository owner/project/branch/provider is assumed, but it contains no unresolved <...> placeholders and hardcodes a specific publisher repository, Keycloak source repository, owner, provider, main refs, and an example.invalid site origin. It passes validate-config. This is not a generic ready-to-fill template; it is a project-specific smoke fixture with misleading setup wording.
reproduction_or_evidence: REPRODUCED: placeholder scan finds no angle placeholders in the file; validate-config exits 0; the concrete URLs and refs are present.
recommended_solution: Rename as a clearly project-specific smoke fixture; correct the header, list every fixed project assumption, and provide a separate fail-closed real-project template with required placeholders.
